FACT_HOOK: Your code sometimes waits before it runs.
FACT_EXPLANATION: Serverless computing promises instant scalability, but there’s a catch that surprised early adopters: the “cold start.” When a function hasn’t been invoked recently, the cloud provider must spin up a fresh execution environment. That setup time—sometimes milliseconds, sometimes seconds—creates a tiny but noticeable delay. It’s the digital equivalent of waking someone from a nap and asking them to sprint. Warm functions respond instantly; cold ones stretch first. Engineers quickly learned to design around this behavior. Some kept functions “warm” with scheduled pings. Others optimized package sizes to reduce initialization time. The irony? In a world marketed as seamless, latency still sneaks in through the back door.
